newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: Burkina Faso calls parliament election for May 11.
newsitem.headline: Burkina Faso calls parliament election for May 11.

text.p: The West African nation of Burkina Faso is to hold parliamentary elections on May 11, the second national elections since it embraced multi-party politics in the early 1990s.

A government statement, issued after a special cabinet meeting late on Friday, also said that electoral lists would be revised from March 5 to 30 by special administrative commissions including representatives of legally recognised parties.
The last parliamentary poll was in 1992.

Burkina Faso's parliament in January scrapped constitutional provisions limiting the presidential mandate to two seven-year terms, a move denounced by the opposition as anti-democratic and a ploy to perpetuate the rule of President Blaise Compaore.
Compaore came to power after a 1987 coup in which his boss, populist leader Captain Thomas Sankara, was killed.
He was the sole candidate in the December 1991 presidential election, a poll boycotted by the opposition and in which almost three quarters of voters abstained.
Burkina Faso and a string of other countries in Africa introduced varying degrees of democratic reform in the early 1990s following the collapse of Soviet-bloc Communism.
Parliament, dominated by Compaore's supporters, also voted in January to increase the number of seats in the national assembly from 107 to 111.
The May election will be run by a national commission but the opposition has denounced its proposed make-up as non-independent.
